approvedDeviation: #872 Tally backend: schema fingerprint moved for two new registered tables (tally_expense_payer, tally_nudge) and four new columns (tally_expense.split_method / split_params_json, tally_group.simplify_opt_in / archived_at), plus a nullable tally_expense.group_id and a tally_expense_line_item that now hangs off the expense with a nullable receipt_id. Export completeness was re-audited in packages/vault/src/gateway/portable-export.ts: both tables are registered in schema/tables.ts so they enter the canonical walk, and exportVault's SELECT * carries every new column with no adapter. All six are ground facts or owner decisions — a restore that dropped them would return expenses nobody paid for, a lost prepared reminder, edits that re-open as exact amounts, a silently re-wired simplification opt-in, or an archived group back in the lists. #872 Locker backend: the fingerprint moved again for five newly registered tables (locker_item_alias, which existed in DDL but was outside the canonical walk, plus locker_item_field, locker_item_address, locker_item_passkey and locker_item_history) and three locker_item changes (password_set_at, archived_at, and a type CHECK widened from six to fifteen item types). Export completeness was re-audited in the same owner file: all five are registered in schema/tables.ts so they enter the walk, and exportVault's SELECT * carries the new columns with no adapter. Every one is a fact the owner entered or a record only this vault holds — an unregistered alias table silently broke every connector binding on restore, and history is the only record that a password was ever rotated. The sidecars' sealed cells (locker_item_field.value_sealed, locker_item_passkey.private_key, locker_item_history.password) stay ciphertext in the artifact exactly like locker_item.password. #873 integration: the fingerprint moved once more for a change inside packages/vault/src/schema/sealed.ts that adds NO table and NO column — the three Locker sidecar sealed columns joined SEALED_PAYLOAD_FIELDS alongside SEALED_COLUMNS, closing a draft-band leak the extended T3 canary caught (a staged import row would have carried a custom field's sealed value, a previous password and a passkey's private key in the clear). Export completeness is unchanged by it and was re-checked anyway: SEALED_PAYLOAD_FIELDS governs sync_import_row payload staging, not the canonical walk, and every one of those cells still leaves exportVault as ciphertext exactly like locker_item.password. #883 authority plane: the fingerprint moved for one new schema module (schema/authority.ts, which adds share_authority and share_delivery_config and drops share_grant, enrich_consent and consent_device.trust in migration rung six) plus the registry, replica-epoch and census edits that ride with it. Export completeness was re-audited in packages/vault/src/gateway/portable-export.ts: both new tables are registered in schema/tables.ts so they enter the canonical walk, the two dropped tables leave it with the storage they named, and every decision either of them held is now a share_authority row. The set of owner decisions the bundle carries is unchanged; only where they live moved. consent_device keeps every identity column and loses only trust, whose value became a device-principal authority row, and exportVault's SELECT * carries all of it with no adapter. share_delivery_config is registered rather than treated as derivable machinery because a restore that dropped it would silently reset a per-grant size ceiling to the vault-wide default. #883 ontology reconciliation: the fingerprint moved again for migration rung seven (schema/reconcile.ts, plus the registry, FTS, atlas, sealed and journal edits that ride with it). Export completeness was re-audited in packages/vault/src/gateway/portable-export.ts and nothing the bundle carried is missing from it. Twelve tables LEAVE the canonical walk and each one's content is still in it: social_contact_card's role line and nickname are people_profile columns (ruling O-contact) and its vcard_rev was a second copy of the row's own updated_at; tally_expense_receipt's rows are core.attachment rows with role='receipt' (ruling O-attach), which the walk already carried; and the ten home.*/business.* tables leave the ontology entirely (ruling O-domains, proposal #885) — the rung REFUSES to run against a vault that holds a row in any of them, so no bundle can lose one. Reach identifiers move from core_party_identifier to social_contact_channel, both registered, so an exported vCard's EMAIL and TEL are read from the channel store rather than the register and the bundle carries the same addresses. Five columns are ADDED and ride exportVault's SELECT * with no adapter: people_profile.nickname and the deleted_at/purge_at trash pairs on core_event and schedule_task (ruling O-trash) — a restore that dropped those would hand back a vault where trashed rows return as live ones. No sealed cell changed class; SEALED_PAYLOAD_FIELDS is now DERIVED from SEALED_COLUMNS (ruling D4c) and the derived set is a strict superset of the hand list it replaces, so every cell that left exportVault as ciphertext still does. #883 entity catalog extract: the fingerprint moved again because VAULT_ENTITIES left schema/tables.ts for schema/entity-catalog.ts (engine W reads the catalog) and entity-labels.test.ts joined the schema-dir hash. No table and no column. Export completeness was re-audited in packages/vault/src/gateway/portable-export.ts: core.share_origin and share.party_vault_binding, the two entities this issue's Docs manifest reads, were already registered and already exported, listVaultEntities is unchanged, and exportVault's SELECT * carries every cell exactly as before.
